clue.text: Traveller may take along this immoral woman

definitions.meaning: luggage, the cases and bags carried on a journey
a dated, disparaging term for a shameless or disreputable woman

explanation.surface: A traveller's companion is cast as a woman of dubious virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a traveller's luggage and, in old-fashioned slang, a woman of loose morals.

clue.text: Important match viewed from a hunting lodge?

definitions.meaning: large animals hunted for sport, such as lions or elephants

explanation.surface: A crucial fixture is watched from a hunters' cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A big game is an important fixture, and the phrase also names large animals hunted as trophies.

clue.text: Good of us to receive half-hearted epicure

parts.note: our means belonging to us

indicators.note: one of the two middle letters, the heart of the word, is lost

parts.note: to meet guests is to receive them

explanation.surface: It is kind of us to welcome a food lover who is only lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an epicure is a connoisseur of fine food and drink.

clue.text: Best people a mate tricked

indicators.note: the letters are tricked out, dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Top performers have played a joke on a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the A-team is the first-choice group, the best people available.

clue.text: Fourth letter in chart — see it any differently? The reason?

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a different order
picks the fourth letter of the word chart

explanation.surface: An eye test asks whether you read the chart differently and why.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain on the eyes is the likely cause of seeing letters wrongly, the reason implied.

clue.text: Artist on track in struggle to survive

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist
to track someone is to trace them

explanation.surface: A painter is set on a trail while fighting to get by.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the rat race is the exhausting competitive struggle of working life.

clue.text: Come back again about aggressive dog

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a cur is a snappy, ill-tempered dog

explanation.surface: A vicious dog keeps returning.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to recur is to happen again, to come back.

clue.text: Adopted children disagreed

parts.note: to adopt a course is to take it, so took
issue is a formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: A family argued over the children they had adopted.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to take issue with someone is to dispute or disagree with them.

clue.text: Gin cocktail swallowed by rising star in French city

indicators.note: the mixed gin goes down inside the star
in a down clue the word for star is read upwards

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A rising celebrity knocks back a gin cocktail on a trip to France.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a city in Provence, once the seat of the popes.

clue.text: Use air differently over a land mass

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over, above, the next
the letters are used in a different order

explanation.surface: Air is exploited in a new way across a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' makes EURASI from USE AIR; in a down clue 'over' sets that above the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined continental land mass of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Fellow eating last of cobbler before cheese

indicators.note: the fellow takes something inside him as if eating it

parts.note: a guy is a fellow, a chap

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word cobbler

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A man munches the end of a shoemaker's work before his cheese course.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm Swiss cheese named after the Gruyères district, so an example of cheese.

clue.text: Beginning to coach more promising staff

indicators.note: the start of the word coach supplies its opening letter

parts.note: rosier prospects are more promising ones

explanation.surface: A coach's early days look brighter for the team staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's hooked pastoral staff, so a particular kind of staff.

clue.text: Graduate twice brought in to reshape one's old school

indicators.note: the doubled graduate is placed inside the word for reshape

parts.note: to alter something is to reshape it

indicators.note: the graduate's abbreviation is repeated to give two copies

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: Two graduates are recruited to revamp the school they attended.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase for the school or university one attended, literally nourishing mother.

clue.text: Novelist in bar? Yes, losing face

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a bar

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A writer drinking in a pub nods in agreement and is embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammond Innes was a British author of thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammond Innes was a popular twentieth-century British thriller writer, an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Additional passage from book court disregarded

indicators.note: the court's letters are ignored and dropped from the passage

parts.note: an extract is a passage taken from a book

explanation.surface: An excerpt from a book is ignored by the court as surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something extra is additional, over and above the usual.

clue.text: Together in the past

explanation.surface: A couple recall being together long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both simultaneously and formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Deep chasm in one area of former Red Sea state

parts.note: an abyss is a bottomless chasm
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A deep gorge lies within a region of an old East African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Old name for Ethiopia, the empire that bordered the Red Sea.

clue.text: Measure criticism after cart overturned

indicators.note: the criticism comes after the cart in the answer
in a down clue the cart is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads
stick is British slang for criticism, as in getting stick

explanation.surface: Blame is gauged after a wagon tips over.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used to measure or judge something.

clue.text: Like a rook initially trapped

definitions.meaning: a chess rook begins the game on a corner square of the board
cornered, with no means of escape

explanation.surface: A chess piece is hemmed in at the start of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooks start on the board's corner squares, and the idiom describes being cornered with no way out.

clue.text: Popular unfounded belief in childhood

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a fancy is a notion with no basis in fact

explanation.surface: A widely held myth dates from one's early years.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: infancy is earliest childhood.

clue.text: Soldier over in Scottish isle is put on trial

indicators.note: the soldier is placed inside the island

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldier is turned over, read upwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier on a Scottish island faces a court.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Nobleman executed? That is strange

indicators.note: beheaded, so the nobleman loses his first letter

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud at the oddness of a lord being put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: eerie means strange and unsettling, uncanny.

clue.text: Ring in extremely remarkable safe

indicators.note: the extremes of the word remarkable, its first and last letters

parts.note: sound means safe, unharmed, as in safe and sound

explanation.surface: A phone rings inside a really impressive strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to resound is to ring out or echo.

clue.text: Market town girl's overacting

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name, with the possessive
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: A young woman puts on a show in a provincial town.
explanation.definitionFit: Evesham is a market town in Worcestershire, England, in the Vale of Evesham.

clue.text: In favour of church showing influence

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Support for the church demonstrates its sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: force here means power or sway over others, influence.

clue.text: Has to step off as quickly as possible

indicators.note: the letters are off, out of place, so they need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get off the step in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb meaning with the utmost speed, from the haste of the old mail riders.

clue.text: I chat over by square in capital

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for chat is turned over, read upwards

parts.note: to rap is to talk informally

explanation.surface: Someone describes chatting by a square in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital of France, an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Suddenly discover successful record playing

parts.note: a hit is a chart-topping record
on means playing, being performed

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a chart-topping song on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to hit on an idea is to discover it suddenly.

clue.text: Senior I upset becomes more rowdy

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly person, once upset, grows louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative synonym: noisier means louder and more boisterous, more rowdy.

clue.text: Out of play though maintaining contact

definitions.meaning: in football or rugby the ball over the touchline is out of play

explanation.surface: A ball goes off the pitch while a player keeps in contact with it.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby and football, touch is the area outside the side lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch is the area beyond the sideline in sport, and the idiom means keeping in contact.

clue.text: Unknown character, crazy having lost head in a New York city

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: the word for crazy drops its first letter

parts.note: bonkers is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A mad stranger has gone wild in a city of New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonkers is a city in Westchester County, New York, just north of the Bronx.

clue.text: Perhaps country family's cat returned holding head of dormouse

parts.note: kin is one's family

indicators.note: the reversed cat holds the extra letter inside it
the word for cat is read backwards

parts.note: mog or moggy is British slang for a cat

indicators.note: the first letter of the word dormouse

explanation.surface: A family pet comes back with a dormouse in its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is one example of a kingdom, hence the qualifying perhaps.
